captions.title: Start with New listing
captions.line: An estate is one listing that holds every house and plot inside it.

captions.title: Press Estate, then name it
captions.line: Estate rather than Home opens a different form. Name the development, not one house in it.

captions.title: Tagline and description
captions.line: What the whole place is, in one line and one paragraph.

captions.title: No Sale or Rent here
captions.line: An estate is sold, not let. Off-plan and the title document say what stage it is at.

captions.title: One row per option
captions.line: A chip adds a row of that shape, and a row is one thing a buyer can pick.

captions.title: Name it, size it, price it
captions.line: A two bedroom bungalow, then a three. Enter moves the caret on.

captions.title: Duplexes, apartments, a terrace
captions.line: The same three fields every time. Enter in a price adds the next size up.

captions.title: A plot needs no name
captions.line: Its size is its name, and the chip puts the caret straight in the square metres.

captions.title: The price nobody typed
captions.line: From 6.8 million, worked out from the cheapest option below.

captions.title: Spread the balance
captions.line: Deposit up front, the rest over so many months. The example uses your cheapest option.

captions.title: Where it is
captions.line: Publishing needs the city and the address.

captions.title: Photos, then save
captions.line: Renders are fine for an off-plan estate, and each option can carry its own.

captions.title: Publish it
captions.line: Then Preview: the site itself, rendering what you just typed. Nothing there is public.

captions.title: Ten options, one page
captions.line: Each with its price and its monthly figure, under one from price.
